newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank says no outflow on lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank says no outflow on lower rates.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza said on Thursday there was no outflow of foreign funds due to recent declines in domestic interest rates.

"We were told investors' money is still here. There is no reason to shift to U.S. dollars," Edeza told Reuters, adding that the peso still enjoys a 3.5 percentage-point interest rate premium over the U.S. dollar.
The peso hit a 27-month low early on Thursday at 26.345 to the dollar. It has been weakening since Tuesday after interest rates fell following last Friday's cut in banks' reserve requirements.
"This is partly speculative. There was also profit-taking on certain positions," Edeza said.
The Central Bank sold less than $15 million early on Thursday to stop the peso from further weakening, Edeza said.
He also denied that the Central Bank was trending towards a depreciation of the peso by raising its dollar offer rate.
"We can decide when to adjust rates. It's a normal Central bank operation. It doesn't mean banks should follow," he said.
Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said separately that the fall in the peso was purely-market driven.
"If you see the peso going up or down, it is likely because of market forces," he told Reuters. "I think the (Central Bank's) strategy will remain the same".
Trading on the foreign exchange market was heavy on Thursday morning, with $188.50 million worth of deals recorded.
The peso average in the morning was at 26.334 versus the previous day's average of 26.318.
